chapter_theme: The fourth part of Pattinathar's Arutpulambal in the woman's voice: she tells her friend that the Lord has mingled with her as river with sea and life with body, and then names him by a chain of similes, gold and its assay, the ruby's light, fire in the flint, the pearl in the shell, sugar in milk, the banyan with countless branches, as the Fullness beyond books, letters, lineage, direction and the five dissolutions, the silent Brahman that burned Kama with a look, present to the awakened and absent to the base.
structure_note: Every unit is two lines closing on the refrain particles அடி, ஆண்டி (ஆன் + அடி: he did, girl) and காண் (see), the address of a woman to her friend (மகடூ முன்னிலை). The couplets alternate between what he did to her (582, 584, 586, 587, 590, 595, 605) and what he is (583, 585, 588, 589, 591, 596 to 604, 606); 592 to 594 turn to who sees him and who does not.

582.reading: Like sea-water and a river run together, I can see no shore; he stood mingled within me like body and life.
582.nuance: Two images of union that cannot be undone: river in sea, life in body. கரை காணேன் (I see no shore) is the woman's own state, not his.

583.reading: As gold is one with the streak that tells its fineness, so is the incomparable Fullness; it is lasting direct experience, like the light inside a ruby.
583.nuance: உரை மாற்று is the assay: the streak a piece of gold leaves on the touchstone and the fineness read from it, which cannot be separated from the gold. அநுபூதி (anubhuti) is the tradition's word for knowing by experience rather than by report.

584.reading: He has no bound and no shore, a ship that never sights land; he is everywhere without measure, and stood as the One.
584.nuance: கரை காணாக் கப்பல் (ship that sees no shore) picks up the woman's கரை காணேன் of 582 and makes it his.

585.reading: The supreme one made of consciousness joined me like a lamp; he has no imagining in him, and wherever I look, all is the Supreme.
585.nuance: தீவகம் is an island, and can also be read as தீபகம், a lamp; joined me like a lamp (giving light) or like an island (set in the sea) both stand. பாவகம் is read as பாவனை, imagining or mental construction; it could also be fire. The last clause is plain.

586.reading: He is within even the innermost; he has no town and no name; he came as the cause that cuts off the thieving senses.
586.nuance: The second line is a formula that recurs: it is the second line of 507 in this work and of Azhuganni 1522, where the first line is that he took the guru's form to cut off birth.

587.reading: Through all those earlier births he sat as grace; in this birth he came, and this one is the true substance.
587.nuance: Grace is said to have been there in every past birth; what is new in this birth is that he came in person (as the guru, 621).

588.reading: Like light on water he fills everything, the one without flaw; like the light of day he spreads everywhere, the Supreme beyond the supreme.
588.nuance: நிராமயன், the one without disease, is a name for the unafflicted Supreme; பராபரன் is the Siddhars' usual name for Brahman.

589.reading: He is subtler than the subtle that no book can grasp; he is the all-pervading Fullness, spread through everything like sugar in milk.
589.nuance: Sugar dissolved in milk is in every drop and visible in none: pervasion without a separate form.

590.reading: Can he be known by the eye of flesh, and not only by the mind's eye? He abides pervading, like the flame-light of a lamp.
590.nuance: ஓருமதோ (can it discern?) is a rhetorical question: only the inner eye sees him.

591.reading: Like the fire-light that lies hidden in a stone, he is the cause of all, and though he lies hidden close within, he is the incomparable Fullness.
591.nuance: புல்லியிருந்தும் can be 'though embracing' or 'though lying lowly and hidden'; both keep the point that nearness and concealment do not make him less.

592.reading: To those in whom awakening has been born he is as fragrance is to a flower of gold; to the base who cannot see him, as fragrance is to a flower of stone.
592.nuance: Neither a gold flower nor a stone flower has scent, so the contrast must lie in the flowers: the gold flower is precious and the awakened add fragrance to it, the stone flower is dead and no fragrance will come. போதம் is bodha, awakening.

593.reading: To those who do not forget him even in confusion, and to the knowers of the cause who have cut off the womb, he becomes a fruit in the hand.
593.nuance: கைக்குள் கனி, the fruit in the palm, is the idiom for what is easily had. The simile of the first line, collyrium-paste and pearl (மைக்குழம்பு முத்து), is obscure: perhaps the pearl showing white against black paste, or the dark and the bright kept together without mixing. கருவறுத்த காரணர் are those who have cut the womb, that is, rebirth.

594.reading: To poets free of attachment he shows like coral seen through crystal; those who take a shell for silver cannot come near him, and will they ever?
594.nuance: Shell taken for silver is the stock Vedantic example of false perception; coral in crystal is seeing through a clear medium. The verse sets clear seeing against mistaken seeing, and makes freedom from attachment the condition of the first.

595.reading: He is not held in a palm-leaf book and is not born of letters; he made all the jackals of the land into fine horses.
595.nuance: The printed நாட்டினரிகள் reads as நாட்டின் அரிகள் (the lions, or Haris, of the land) but the sense needs நரிகள், jackals: the Madurai sport in which Siva turned jackals into horses for the Pandya. Two lines set the Lord outside books and letters and inside legend.

596.reading: He outlasts even the fivefold dissolution; he is the one with poison held in his throat and fire in his eye.
596.nuance: பஞ்சப் பிரளயம், the five dissolutions, is a traditional count of the ends of the world; the epithets are Siva's, the poison drunk at the churning and the third eye.

597.reading: He guards within and without; from the measureless cosmos onward he guards the world, and guards the ten directions no eye can see.
597.nuance: Protection, the second of the five acts, is given four scopes: inner, outer, the worlds, the directions.

598.reading: He is the Brahman that does not speak, the great light beyond speech, the great light that desire and the bonds cannot come near.
598.nuance: பேசாப் பிரமம் (the Brahman that does not speak) is the refrain-name this part of the work gives him (606, 610); the silence is his, not the devotee's.

599.reading: He has passed beyond country; he is the clear sea that has passed beyond direction; he is the substance so solid that not even a needle's point can be pressed into it.
599.nuance: ஊசிமுனை ஊன்ற இல்லா is fullness as density: there is no gap anywhere in him for anything else.

600.reading: He is the pearl's light within the shell; to those who lack the gaze of consciousness he is the rare substance that stays unseen, like light in water.
600.nuance: Both images are of a light that is present but not seen unless one looks rightly; சின்மய நோக்கு, the gaze of consciousness, is what 611 says the Lord gave her.

601.reading: He is the banyan tree with branches beyond number; he is the true substance whose higher states pierce through the sky.
601.nuance: மேலாம் பதங்கள் may be the higher padas, the states or worlds above, or his feet (பதம்); the banyan is the tree under which Siva teaches and the tree that spreads from one seed, as in Sivavakkiyar.

602.reading: His flower-feet have passed beyond every lineage and cling to none; he is the rare substance that searched everywhere like a goad.
602.nuance: வங்கிஷம் (வம்சம்) is lineage or clan; the Lord is outside caste and descent. அங்குஷம் is the elephant-goad; 'as a goad searched everywhere' may mean that he drives and governs all, or the word may be corrupt.

603.reading: Name has been lost, there is no place from which to tell it; he is the cause who opened his fire-eye to burn Kama with a look.
603.nuance: நாம நட்டம் is the loss of name: his, as the nameless one of 586, or hers, as the self that no longer has a name to speak from (617, 612). The burning of Kama is set beside the loss of name, desire and ego ending together.

604.reading: He is red gold never beaten, a pearl never dived for, on a branch no hand can reach, the honey-nectar no fly has entered.
604.nuance: Four images of what is unmade and untouched: gold not worked, pearl not fished, a branch out of reach, honey no fly has spoiled. The Lord is uncreated and unsullied.

605.reading: As one tests a bit of gold on the stone against the standard needle and says what its fineness is, so he set me against the standard, joined me to it and took me in whole.
605.nuance: ஆணி is the touch-needle, the set of gold needles of known fineness against which a streak is compared; அடங்கல் இட்டு is 'included entirely'. The image of 583 returns as what he did to her: she was assayed and absorbed. The syntax is compressed and the agent of each verb is not certain.

606.reading: Though the beings of the measureless cosmos are so many, he does not say even a splinter's worth, not at all: the Brahman that does not speak.
606.nuance: The silence is total and the audience is total; the Lord does not explain himself to anyone.

links.note: Azhuganni's stanza has the same two formulas, the guru's form taken to cut off birth and the cause come to cut the thieving senses, with the refrain ஆத்தாடி; the line is shared property of the pulambal tradition, not one poet's.

Both make the lowest understanding a mistake of perception: the Kural's paltry mind takes what does not last for what lasts; Pattinathar's shell-for-silver people cannot reach the Lord. The Kural's object is impermanence, Pattinathar's the Supreme.

Tirumular ends speech in the pure form beyond the three voids; Pattinathar's Lord is the Brahman that does not speak and the great light past speech. In both the end of words belongs to the Supreme itself.

Tirumular's disciples become the reality mixed in the shoreless light as ghee mixes in pure milk; Pattinathar's Fullness is spread through all as sugar in milk. Same vessel, but Tirumular's image is of the soul merging and Pattinathar's of the Lord pervading.

The Kural makes the Primal Lord first of the world as the letter A is first of letters; Pattinathar says he is not born of letters and not held in a book. Not a conflict, since the Kural's letter is a simile, but Pattinathar refuses the medium the Kural uses.

source_issues: 586 line 2 (கள்ளப்புலனறுக்கக்காரணமாய்வந்தாண்டி) is also line 2 of 507 (arutpulambal-2:2); the work carries two numbering runs, the short numbers 1 onward and the long ids 0276_01-NN, and units recur between them.
595 நாட்டினரிகள்: the sense (the Madurai jackals-into-horses sport) needs நரிகள், jackals; the printed split gives அரிகள்.
The units of this work are printed without word-spacing, so several readings (585 தீவகம்/பாவகம், 602 அங்குஷம், 605) turn on where words are divided.
